title: Session resilience fuzzing and observability journal
content:
Purpose:
Keep a running lab notebook for experiment ideas + config sketches for a lightweight fuzzing harness that stresses session lifecycle (snapshots, offload/restore, prefetch, eviction) and captures targeted telemetry to find resilience gaps. Personal scratchpad — not yet a PRD.

Goals:
- Surface edge cases that cause session corruption or silent data loss when interrupted during KV cache ops or snapshotting.
- Validate observability signals are sufficient to triage (span traces, sample payloads, session-delta diffs).
- Prototype a minimal harness we can run in staging that injects network faults, SIGTERM, and storage flakiness.

Assumptions:
- Harness sits next to the ingress test runner and can orchestrate 1000 short sessions concurrently (spikes).
- We can sample full session diffs for 1% of failures (storage cost acceptable for staging).

High-level architecture (ascii):

  [test-orchestrator] ---> [ingress-sim] --> [runtime-proxy] --> [gpu-runner]
                                     |                     \-> [kv-cache]
                                     |                      \-> [snapshot-store]
                                     v
                            [fault-injector / network shim]

Fault types to inject:
- mid-token SIGTERM on GPU worker (simulate OOM preemption)
- delayed snapshot write (NFS timeout / 500ms-5s)
- transient KV cache read errors (404/timeout)
- ingress retry storms (duplicated messages)

Telemetry shape (proposal) -- flattened JSON lines to ingestion:
- event_type: string (session_start|session_end|snapshot_write|kv_read|kv_write|fallback)
- session_id: string
- trace_id: string
- timestamp_iso: string
- step: string (ingress, proxy, runtime, storage)
- outcome: string (ok|timeout|error|fallback)
- error_class: string (optional)
- sample_blob_ref: string (optional pointer to stored session-diff)
- numeric_counters: list of short counters like ["tokens_generated:34","kv_reads:3"]

Note: flattened lines -> easier to stream to kinesis/otel ingest. Keep fields conservative to avoid cardinality explosion.

Example telemetry ingestion API (sketch):
POST /telemetry/v1/events
headers: x-rw-auth: token, content-type: application/json
body: {
  "event_type": "snapshot_write",
  "session_id": "s-4f3b",
  "trace_id": "t-8734",
  "timestamp_iso": "2025-12-03T12:11:02Z",
  "step": "storage",
  "outcome": "timeout",
  "error_class": "nfs-timeout",
  "numeric_counters": ["snapshot_bytes:12488"]
}

Sampling strategy (cheap but useful):
- deterministic sampling: every Nth snapshot write per tenant (N configurable by tenant)
- failure-centric up-sampling: on outcome!=ok, capture full session diff and increase sampling for that session id for next M events

Fuzz runner config sketch (yaml-like):
- concurrency: 250
- session_duration_mean_ms: 6000
- noise_profile: bursty|steady|interactive
- fault_matrix:
  - name: sigterm-mid-token
    probability: 0.002
    target: gpu-runner
  - name: snapshot-latency
    probability: 0.01
    latency_ms: 300-3000
  - name: kv-404
    probability: 0.003

Observability checks / heatmap metrics to render in console:
- session-fidelity-loss-rate (percent of sessions that diverge from expected golden replay)
- snapshot-latency-95, -99
- kv-read-error-rate by tenant and by API path
- time-to-first-fallback (ms)
- failure-to-diff-sample (ratio)

Playbook (triage flow):
1) alert on fidelity-loss-rate > threshold -> open incident (auto-attach last 20 failure diffs).
2) if snapshot-latency spikes, run targeted snapshot-latency stress test (replicate with harness).
3) if kv-read-errors concentrated on proxy step, increase proxy retries and add idempotency guards.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to securely store sampled session diffs (PII risk): need automated scrubber or deterministic redaction rules. (cc: security)
- Cost: storing diffs for 1% of failures across staging might still be $$$ — need quotas.
- Can we reuse existing telemetry ingestion (otel/gateway) or do we need a side channel?
- Should the harness drive both HTTP and streaming gRPC paths? (prefer both)

Next small experiments (week-of):
- build minimal harness that can flip SIGTERM and record ingestion events (P0)
- wire a cheap dashboard in console for snapshot-latency-percentiles (P1)
- draft scrubber rules prototype and run on sample diffs (P1)

Notes to self:
- Log span ids in human-readable short form in failure emails so oncall can correlate quickly.
- Keep sample_blob_ref pointers TTLed for 7 days and delete automatically.
- Talk to Priya about quota and tenant tagging for fuzz runs.

References / links:
- GH PR for related runtime instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842
- Slack thread: #runtime-fuzzing (search: "fuzz harness ideas", Feb 2025)
- Jira: RINF-2176 (fuzzing spike for session lifecycle)

End of scratchpad. This is messy — still thinking through tradeoffs.
